청소.x: I cleaned my room on the weekend.

농구.x: I played basketball in the school gym.

등.ex: 하루 종일 컴퓨터를 해서 등이 아파요.
등.x: I've been on the computer all day, so my back hurts.
등.e: Homonym warning: 등 also means 'lamp' and 'etc.' (and so on).
등.t: For lower-back pain Koreans usually say 허리가 아파요, not 등이 아파요.

결혼식.x: My older sister's wedding is next month.
결혼식.t: Guests usually give cash in an envelope (축의금) instead of buying a registry gift.

십만.ex: 어제 백화점에서 십만 원짜리 운동화를 샀어요.
십만.x: Yesterday I bought sneakers that cost 100,000 won at the department store.
십만.e: Literally 'ten ten-thousands' — Korean counts big numbers in units of 10,000.

약하다.m: to be weak, to be frail; to be mild
약하다.x: I was physically weak as a child.
약하다.e: Literally 'weak'; careful — 약 meaning 'medicine' is a different word.

덕분.ex: 선생님 덕분에 한국어 실력이 많이 늘었어요.
덕분.x: Thanks to my teacher, my Korean has improved a lot.
덕분.e: Literally 'a share of virtue' — benefiting from someone's goodness.
덕분.t: Use 덕분에 for good results; for bad ones use 때문에 or 탓에.

엽서.ex: 여행 중에 친구에게 예쁜 엽서를 보냈어요.
엽서.x: I sent my friend a pretty postcard while traveling.
엽서.e: Literally 'leaf writing', a message on a single thin sheet.
엽서.t: Pronounced [엽써]: the ㅅ becomes tense after the ㅂ batchim.

업무.x: I have a lot of work today, so I'm leaving late.
업무.t: Pronounced [엄무] — nasalization; 업무 sounds formal, while everyday speech just uses 일.

생산되다.m: to be produced, to be manufactured
생산되다.x: This car is produced in Korea.

상인.ex: 시장 상인들이 아침 일찍 가게 문을 열어요.
상인.x: The market vendors open their shops early in the morning.

상담하다.m: to consult, to get counseling, to counsel
상담하다.x: I talked with my homeroom teacher about my career plans.

앙코르.ex: 관객들이 앙코르를 외치자 가수가 다시 나왔어요.
앙코르.x: When the audience shouted for an encore, the singer came back out.
앙코르.t: 앙코르 공연 can also mean extra shows added because of demand.

짱.forms: 짱이에요 · 짱이다 · 짱 + adjective (짱 좋아요 = super good)
짱.m: the best, awesome; super, really (before adjectives)
짱.x: The tteokbokki here is seriously the best!
짱.e: Often linked to 장 (長) 'head, chief', said with a tense consonant for emphasis; the origin is not certain.
짱.t: Casual. A thumbs-up with 짱! means 'the best!'. Also found in compounds like 얼짱 'great-looking (literally face-best)'.

고등학생.x: Korean high school students study until late at night.

녹지.ex: 도시에 녹지가 많으면 사람들이 더 건강해져요.
녹지.x: When a city has lots of green space, people become healthier.
녹지.t: Pronounced [녹찌]: ㅈ becomes tense after the ㄱ batchim.

망설이다.x: He hesitated for a long time over whether to confess his feelings.
망설이다.t: Often used with -(으)ㄹ까 말까: 갈까 말까 망설이다 'to go back and forth about going'.

얼핏.forms: 얼핏 + perception verb: 얼핏 보다, 얼핏 듣다, 얼핏 보기에
얼핏.m: at a glance, briefly, in passing
얼핏.ex: 얼핏 보면 두 사람이 쌍둥이 같아요.
얼핏.x: At a glance, the two of them look like twins.

역시나.ex: 역시나 오늘도 지하철이 사람으로 꽉 찼어요.
역시나.x: As expected, the subway was packed with people again today.
역시나.e: 역시 'also, as expected' + emphatic -나; stresses that it happened just as predicted.

위태롭다.x: That company's business situation is precarious.
위태롭다.e: Literally 'dangerous and perilous' plus -롭다 'having the quality'.

머리를 식히다.forms: 머리를 식혀요 · 머리를 식혔어요 · 머리 좀 식히고 올게요
머리를 식히다.m: to clear one's head, to take a mental break
머리를 식히다.x: I took a short walk in the park to clear my head.
머리를 식히다.e: 식히다 = to cool down; literally 'to cool off the head.'
머리를 식히다.t: Pronounced [시키다]: ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

손을 놓다.forms: 손을 놓아요(놔요) · 손을 놓았어요 · 일손을 놓다
손을 놓다.m: to stop working on, to give up on; to let go (of a hand)
손을 놓다.ex: 그는 사업이 실패한 뒤 모든 일에서 손을 놓았어요.
손을 놓다.x: After his business failed, he gave up on everything.
손을 놓다.e: Literally 'to put down one's hands' and stop working.
손을 놓다.t: Also literal: 제 손을 놓지 마세요, 'Don't let go of my hand.'

콧대가 높다.forms: 콧대가 높아요 · 콧대가 높았어요 · 콧대를 꺾다 (to humble)
콧대가 높다.m: to be stuck-up, to be arrogant, to be proud
콧대가 높다.ex: 그 배우는 인기가 많아서 콧대가 높아요.
콧대가 높다.x: That actor is so popular that he's stuck-up.
콧대가 높다.e: 콧대 = the bridge of the nose; a high nose bridge symbolizes pride.
콧대가 높다.t: Pronounced [코때]: the 사이시옷 makes the ㄷ tense.

정비.ex: 정부는 낡은 법과 제도를 정비하기로 했습니다.
정비.x: The government decided to overhaul outdated laws and systems.
정비.e: Literally 'arrange and equip'; also means vehicle maintenance, as in 자동차 정비.

제조업.ex: 한국 경제에서 제조업은 아주 중요한 역할을 합니다.
제조업.x: Manufacturing plays a very important role in the Korean economy.

적대시하다.m: to regard as an enemy, to be hostile toward
적대시하다.ex: 두 나라는 오랫동안 서로를 적대시해 왔습니다.
적대시하다.x: The two countries have long regarded each other as enemies.

당돌하다.m: bold, forward, cheeky (especially for a young person)
당돌하다.ex: 어린 학생이 사장님에게 당돌하게 질문을 했어요.
당돌하다.x: A young student boldly asked the company president a question.
당돌하다.e: Literally 'abrupt and sudden' — acting without the expected deference.
당돌하다.t: Can be admiring or critical depending on tone: a 당돌한 신입 is a gutsy, unintimidated newcomer.

우호적.ex: 두 나라는 오랫동안 우호적인 관계를 유지해 왔습니다.
우호적.x: The two countries have maintained friendly relations for a long time.

줄곧.m: all along, the whole time, constantly
줄곧.ex: 그는 아침부터 줄곧 컴퓨터 앞에 앉아 있었어요.
줄곧.x: He's been sitting in front of the computer ever since this morning.
줄곧.e: Probably 줄 'line' plus 곧다 'straight' — going on in one unbroken line.

덧없이.x: My youth passed by all too fleetingly.
덧없이.e: 덧 is an old word for a brief moment; compare 어느덧 'before you know it'.
덧없이.t: Pronounced [더덥씨]; 덧없는 인생 'fleeting life' is a classic phrase.

천체물리학.x: She is majoring in astrophysics in graduate school.

등단.m: literary debut, debut as a writer
등단.x: She won the New Year's literary contest and debuted as a poet.
등단.e: Literally 'ascending the platform' — stepping onto the literary stage.
등단.t: Usually used as 등단하다; 'X(으)로 등단하다' means to debut as X, e.g. 시인으로, 소설가로.

역사소설.ex: 이 역사소설은 조선 시대 궁궐을 배경으로 해요.
역사소설.x: This historical novel is set in a Joseon-era royal palace.

박탈하다.m: to deprive of, to strip of (rights, a title)
박탈하다.x: That athlete was stripped of his medal for doping.
박탈하다.t: Often passive with 당하다: 자격을 박탈당하다 = to be stripped of one's qualification.

지속가능성.ex: 요즘 기업들은 지속가능성을 경영의 핵심으로 삼고 있습니다.
지속가능성.x: These days companies make sustainability central to their management.
지속가능성.e: Literally 'the quality of being able to continue'; -성 = '-ness, -ity'.
지속가능성.t: Pronounced [지속까능썽]: 가 and 성 become tense.

작금.m: these days, the present time, recently
작금.x: The current economic situation is very difficult.
작금.t: Mostly in formal writing and news as 작금의 + noun 'the present ~'.
